claims.statement: Tom Allen was born at Birmingham, England, on April 23, 1839.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen was born at Birmingham, Engiand, April 23, 1839

claims.statement: Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist, died early on the morning of April 5, 1903, at the Baptist Hospital.
claims.excerpt: retired champion pugilist of the world. died early yesterday morning

claims.statement: Allen's funeral was expected on Wednesday morning, April 8, 1903, from his home over No. 615 Market Street.

claims.statement: Allen was proprietor of The Champion's Rest at No. 615 Market Street (other papers print 619).
claims.excerpt: proprietor of “The Champion's Rest” at No. 615 Market strect

claims.statement: For years Allen personally ran the Champion's Rest, presiding at the piano and directing the nightly concert.
claims.excerpt: personally conducted the affairs of the “Champion's Rest.”

claims.statement: After returning from England, Allen came to America, settled in St. Louis and opened a saloon he named The Champion's Rest.
claims.excerpt: Ho then came to America and locating in St. Louls opened a saloon

claims.statement: As of April 1903 The Champion's Rest was the headquarters of the Albion Social Club and was known as a resort for the city's poor with no place to sleep.
claims.excerpt: is to-day one of the most notorious resorts in the city

claims.statement: Allen's silver cup, presented to him in England and known as the Champion Boxing Cup of England, stood on the back bar of the Rest.
claims.excerpt: is a silver cup which was presented to Allen in England

claims.statement: Allen was the only man in ring history, during the bare-knuckle era, to lose the championship and regain it.
claims.excerpt: was the only man in the history of the ring during the time when no gloves

claims.statement: Allen insisted on the title of champion; any fan who called him the ex-champion had to settle with him.
claims.excerpt: any fan who dared call him the “ex-champion”

claims.statement: Allen was robbed of money or decisions in several battles, and twice opponents' friends broke into the ring and forced him to give in under threat of revolvers.
claims.excerpt: Allen fought several battles in which he was robbed either of the money or the decision

claims.statement: Allen came to America as the champion of England in 1869.
claims.excerpt: He came to America as the champion of England in 1869

claims.statement: Allen returned to England on May 6, 1877.

claims.statement: Allen took to his bed about six weeks before his death, around late February 1903, and was given the best of attention.

notes: Long life summary with a full bout table (24 bouts). Printed years are OCR-damaged in several table lines (180, 184, 185, 195, 1968, 1895, 1839 for the Sullivan remark); those are given as low confidence and in notes. The 1869 win over Bill Davis and the 1873 Hogan bout are both in the table. The 1872 vs 1873 McCool date conflicts with the narrative. Mrs. Taylor is 'Mary' here and 'Polly' in 204. Mrs. Hartgrove's husband and the Kelly-seconds detail were left out as minor.
